messages.content: How does in-context learning work in LLMs?

In-context learning: the model uses examples provided in the prompt to infer a pattern and apply it to a new case — without any gradient updates or weight changes. Mechanism: unclear but likely the attention mechanism allows the model to 'simulate' gradient descent within the forward pass itself, using the examples as implicit training signal. Practically: few-shot prompting (providing 3-5 examples of the desired behaviour) dramatically improves performance on structured tasks. Chain-of-thought prompting (providing step-by-step reasoning examples) activates the model's latent reasoning capabilities. Zero-shot performance improves when the model has been instruction-tuned (trained to follow instructions without examples).
What is the architecture of a decoder-only language model like TitanAI?

Decoder-only models (GPT architecture): process tokens left to right using causal (masked) self-attention — each token can only attend to previous tokens, not future ones. This enables autoregressive generation: the model predicts one token at a time, each prediction conditioned on all previous tokens. Architecture layers: embedding layer (token + positional), N transformer blocks (each containing masked multi-head self-attention + feed-forward network + layer norm + residual connections), and a final linear projection to vocabulary logits followed by softmax. The model is trained by predicting the next token across billions of examples — a deceptively simple objective that produces remarkably general capabilities.
How does a transformer model work?

Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017): the architecture underlying GPT, BERT, and all modern large language models. Key mechanism: self-attention. For each token, attention computes a weighted sum of all other tokens' representations, weighted by relevance. This allows the model to relate any word to any other word regardless of distance — solving the problem of long-range dependencies that crippled RNNs. Components: token embeddings, positional encodings (giving the model position information), multi-head attention layers (multiple attention patterns in parallel), feed-forward networks, layer normalisation, and residual connections. Decoder-only models (GPT) generate text left to right. Encoder models (BERT) process full context bidirectionally.
What is the difference between supervised, self-supervised, and reinforcement learning from human feedback?

Supervised learning: model trained on labelled input-output pairs. Requires expensive human annotation. Self-supervised learning: model generates its own labels from unlabelled data — GPT-style pretraining (predict next token) is self-supervised. Cheap and scalable to massive datasets. RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback): after pretraining, humans rank model outputs, a reward model is trained on those rankings, and the language model is fine-tuned via RL to maximise the reward model's score. This aligns the model's outputs with human preferences. The sequence for modern LLMs: pretraining (self-supervised on internet text) → SFT (supervised fine-tuning on curated data) → RLHF or DPO (alignment to human preferences).
What is emergent capability in large language models?

Emergent capabilities: abilities that appear suddenly and were not present at smaller model scales, and were not explicitly trained for. Examples: chain-of-thought reasoning, few-shot learning, arithmetic, coding, and translation emerged in models above certain parameter thresholds without being directly trained. Significance: we cannot reliably predict what a larger model will be able to do — capabilities emerge discontinuously. This makes scaling unpredictable but also suggests capabilities we haven't discovered yet. The implication for AI safety: a model might be benign at one scale and capable of qualitatively different (and potentially dangerous) behaviours at a larger scale.
